A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same C&P knowledge-conflict research, despite substantial methodological and experimental revisions. Text, equations, tables, and figures support comparison throughout. v1 ends with references; v2 includes a readable Appendix A.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of five MLLMs, fine-tuning results, component ablations, and qualitative cases in Sections 3–5 and Tables 2–6.

after.justification: v2 reports original baseline and fine-tuning evaluations, component ablations, and conflict-pattern analyses in Sections 3–5 and Appendix A.

M1.justification: v1's three-stage generator-validator training uses perception consistency, cognition consistency, and a connector that selects answer-containing boxes. v2 replaces this procedure with C&P link tokens added to the vocabulary and a redesigned connector that verifies correct answers and corrects GPT-4o-generated erroneous answers. Section 4 specifies a substantially different training set and response construction.

E1.justification: The benchmark suite drops Kleister Charity and WikiTableQuestions and adds single-page DUDE examples spanning medical, legal, technical, and financial documents. DocVQA, DeepForm, FUNSD, and ChartQA remain. This removes dedicated table-QA coverage and changes the represented document domains, rather than merely changing sample counts.

E2.justification: Qwen-VL-Chat is replaced by Qwen2.5-VL-7b. More substantially, the main open-model comparisons replace original-weight comparators with supervised fine-tuned SFT-baselines. Original-weight InternVL2 results remain as diagnostics in v2 Table 9, but no longer serve as the principal fine-tuning comparators. GPT-4o and Qwen-VL-Max remain evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 replaces keyword filtering and answer-text matching with GPT-4o-assisted filtering and semantic box localization, corrects DeepForm page assignments, and applies red-box visual prompting to open models as well as closed models. Evaluation samples and API snapshots change. It also switches reported averages from micro- to macro-averaging and introduces Idealized C&P Consistency while dropping separate generator-validator consistency metrics.

E4.justification: v1's three-component Qwen-VL-Chat ablation is replaced by InternVL2-2b link-token/connector ablations covering consistency and task accuracy, including Appendix A.5. v2 adds manual inspection of 10% of inconsistent cases, a conflict taxonomy, and before/after conflict-pattern analysis. Its cases include a persistent cognitive failure; the earlier postcode example reappears with different model attribution.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. v2's deterministic-inference disclosure and conditional consistency metric do not introduce statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Results are extensively replaced and supplemented. InternVL2-2b's baseline/fine-tuned averages are 12.09/49.94 in v1 Table 3 and 76.40/80.12 in v2 Table 1, under different training and evaluation conditions. These are not same-setting gains. v2 adds idealized-consistency and conflict-pattern results; its Table 2 reports task improvements throughout, whereas v1 Table 6 includes some cognitive-task declines.

T1.justification: v2 defines Idealized C&P Consistency by restricting evaluation to pairs whose two responses each achieve ANLS of at least 0.5 against ground truth. It drops the separate generator-validator consistency definitions. The basic C&P averaging and containment equations remain unchanged, and neither version provides theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The central identification of C&P conflicts remains, but v2 adds annotation noise as an asserted cause in the abstract and introduction and redefines the mitigation contribution around link tokens and cross-verification. It removes v1's headline claim of at least 34% consistency improvement and strengthens the task-performance claim from improvement in most scenarios to improvement across the reported settings.

C2.justification: v2 introduces annotation heterogeneity and semantic bias as explanations for conflicts and identifies instruction-following failures as confounds in original-weight evaluations. It adds an explicit inability to overcome fundamental cognitive limitations and qualifications about representing cognition/perception solely through VQA/OCR. v1's discussion accepting consistent-but-incorrect outputs as a trade-off is removed.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds detailed preprocessing, page-selection, evaluation, and synthetic-error prompts, plus specific API snapshots. Basic training hyperparameters and hardware remain documented. However, v2 omits constructed training-set counts comparable to those in v1 and replaces the named Duguang OCR engine with a generic commercial solution. Its data-release statement promises future availability without providing access.

R1.justification: v2 selectively updates references, adding VisionLLM v2, newer model/dataset papers, and recent cross-modal conflict studies while removing generic MLLM references. Generator-validator work remains cited but loses its central methodological role, and the claim that previous conflict research concerns only text disappears. The central C&P novelty framing and most related-work themes remain.

P1.justification: The narrative is extensively rewritten and reorganized. Dataset descriptions and construction details move into Appendix A, the method gains component subsections, task-performance discussion moves before ablations, and related work is condensed. v2 adds a standalone Limitations section and removes the Reproducibility Statement, alongside substantial introduction and explanatory revisions.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column preprint formatting to two columns. The method diagram is redrawn, conflict-distribution graphics are added, and result tables are restructured to display ordinary and idealized consistency together. Ablations span main-text and appendix tables, the sample-construction illustration is relocated and updated, and extensive prompt tables are introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves evaluation validity by addressing instruction-following confounds through SFT-baselines and uniform visual prompting, and by correcting the reported DeepForm page-assignment problem. Component ablations, conflict analyses, failure evidence, and detailed appendix prompts make the findings more assessable. These gains outweigh reduced benchmark coverage and missing training-set counts. The stronger attribution of conflicts to annotation noise remains indirectly supported, but the improved controls resolve an important weakness in v1's evidence for its central intervention.
